title: Schotter drift
label: A lattice of squares where order and disorder trade places in drifting patches, some squares opening into nested ones, while slow rings of order cross the sheet.

title: Tesseract
label: A hypercube turning in four dimensions, projected to a fan of fine lines where only a seeded subset of its edges is drawn.

title: Ribbon sheaf
label: One looping curve copied a few hundred times, each copy turned slightly further, so the hairlines build a folded translucent ribbon.

title: Pegs and string
math: chord from peg i to peg (k * i) mod N for every peg i; k sweeps continuously from 2 up to 2 + range and back, lingering near whole numbers (cardioid at 2, nephroid at 3, then 3, 4 and 5 cusps)
label: Pegs on a ring, each joined by a straight thin string to the peg at k times its number, while k sweeps slowly so the glowing envelope curves (cardioid, nephroid and more) bloom and fold into one another.

title: Metamorphosis
label: A sheet of hatched and empty tiles that interlock without gaps and drift sideways; their edge curves change from one shape family to another as they cross the page.

title: Harmonograph
math: x(u) = Σ A_i sin(f_i u + φ_i) m_i(u), y(u) likewise; f_i = a_i N + e_i integers, m_i(u) = 0.55 + 0.45 cos(k_i u + ψ_i), u in [0, 2π]
label: One closed pen path from four pendulums with near-integer frequency ratios; a periodic amplitude envelope winds the spiral in and out and the ink gathers where the path retraces.

title: Strange attractors
math: Aizawa: dx/dt = (z - b) x - d y, dy/dt = d x + (z - b) y, dz/dt = c + a z - z^3/3 - (x^2 + y^2)(1 + e z) + f z x^3;  Thomas: dx/dt = sin y - b x (cyclic);  Halvorsen: dx/dt = -a x - 4 y - 4 z - y^2 (cyclic)
label: A swarm of particles gliding along a strange attractor, each with a short comet trail; the flow slowly changes its parameters and every few epochs the swarm melts into a different attractor.

title: Chladni figure
math: u = cos t (cos n pi x cos m pi y - cos m pi x cos n pi y) + sin t (same with n', m');  sand on u = 0, contours at u = +-0.15, +-0.3
label: The standing-wave pattern of a square plate drawn as contours of the displacement, with sand collecting on the lines where the plate stays still while two vibration modes cross-fade.

title: Hyperbolic tiling
math: {p,q} tiling of the Poincare disc; geodesics are circle arcs orthogonal to |z|=1; z -> (z + a)/(1 + conj(a) z), a(theta) a closed orbit
label: A regular tiling of the hyperbolic plane drawn in the Poincare disc: pentagons and heptagons shrink toward the rim while a moving Mobius shift makes the whole tiling swim like a fisheye.

title: Apollonian gasket
math: k4 = k1 + k2 + k3 +- 2 sqrt(k1k2 + k2k3 + k3k1); circles move by z -> (z - a)/(1 - conj(a) z), a(theta) a closed orbit
label: An Apollonian gasket, the packing of tangent circles generated by Descartes' theorem, swirled by a Mobius map that carries every circle to another exact circle and keeps all tangencies.

title: Penrose phason drift
math: x.e_j + g_j in Z, e_j = (cos 2pi j/5, sin 2pi j/5), sum g_j = 0; rhomb vertices sum_m K_m e_m, K_m = ceil(x.e_m + g_m); g_j = g0_j + A cos(theta + 4 pi j/5)
label: A Penrose rhomb tiling generated from a pentagrid whose lines slowly slide, so tiles flip in place while the pattern stays a perfect Penrose tiling.

title: Roulette rosette
math: x = (R-r) cos u + d cos(((R-r)/r) u), y = (R-r) sin u - d sin(((R-r)/r) u), R/r = a/b rational; d stepped per copy
label: A hypotrochoid drawn ninety times, each copy with the pen offset a little larger and the copy turned a little further, so the copies weave moire rosettes.

title: Roos
math: r = cos(k t), t in [0, 4 pi), k = p/q in {5/2, 4}, blended in polar form r = (1-L) r_a + L r_b; copy j: scale 1 - 0.92 j/N, turn j d, petal exponent 1 + 0.9 j/N
label: One rose r = cos(kt) copied about forty times, each copy smaller, turned a little further and with slimmer petals, so the hairlines build a translucent lotus while k slides between rational values.

title: Droste
math: z = exp(w), w = G (u1 + rho u2), G = 2 pi i / (n1 + n2 rho); the cube pattern is periodic in u, shifted by tau (k1,k2), tau = t/T, so tau = 1 is the identity
label: A field of pencil-hatched cubes in three tones, wound into a logarithmic spiral that contains a smaller twisted copy of itself and zooms endlessly inward, after the Droste effect and Escher's Print Gallery.

title: Kubus
math: h(i,j) in 0..n, h(i,j) >= h(i+1,j), h(i,j) >= h(i,j+1); the hexagon n x n x n is tiled by 3n^2 rhombi; a flip of three rhombi adds or removes one cube
label: An isometric stack of cubes in a corner, drawn as a pencil tiling of rhombi in three tones; cubes are added and removed one at a time so the heap grows, collapses and builds towers and canyons.

title: Trap
math: cell (a,b) = projection of cube (x,y,z) with a = x - z, b = y - z; flights step (0,-1), (-1,0), (0,1), (1,0); the cells close, the depths x+y+z (the paint order) do not
label: A square ring of isometric cubes drawn as a pencil staircase in three tones: four flights, each rising into the next, so the stairs climb for ever; a light sweep and four small marks circle round it.
